mechaber.he:
דין בכור שנתערב ומת אחד מהבהמות. ובו ג' סעיפים:
שנים שהפקידו אצל אחד שני זכרים אחד בכור וא' פשוט ומת אחד מהם ואינו יודע איזה (מת) מניח הנשאר ביניהם והוא בין שניהם ודינו כספק בכור:
mechaber.en:
The law of a firstborn that became mixed and one of the animals died. In it are 3 seifim.
Two people who deposited with one person two males—one a firstborn and one ordinary—and one of them died and it is unknown which died—they leave what remains between them, and it is between both of them and its law is like a doubtful firstborn.

turei_zahav.he: והוא בין שניהם. רצונו לומר בין הכהן ובין מי שהפקיד הפשוט וכשיפול בו מום יחלקו בין שניהם אלו:
turei_zahav.en: He is among both. He would like to say between the priest and the man who is the simple clerk and when he falls, he will be divided between them:

baer_heitev.he: שניהם. ר"ל בין הכהן ובין מי שהפקיד הפשוט וכשיפול בו מום יחלקו בין שניהם אלו. ט"ז:
baer_heitev.en: Both of them. Meaning both the Kohen and the one who deposited the ordinary animal, and when a blemish falls in it they shall divide between these two. Taz.

beer_hagolah.en: This is straightforward from the Gemara, Bechorot 18b.

mechaber.he: מי שהפקיד בכור אצל חבירו ולחבירו פשוט (פי' שאינו בכור) ומת אחד מהם המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה וכיון שהנפקד מוחזק יחזיקנו ויאכלנו במומו:
mechaber.en: One who deposited a firstborn with his fellow and his fellow had an ordinary animal (meaning: not a firstborn), and one of them died—the burden of proof is on the one who extracts from his fellow; and since the depositor is in possession, he retains it and eats it in its blemished state.

turei_zahav.he: וכיון שהנפקד מוחזק כו'. פירוש שיכול לומר לכהן הבא להוציא ממנו שהבכור מת וזה הנשאר הוא הפשוט ועל כן הוה הכהן המוציא מחבירו ועליו הראיה:
turei_zahav.en: It is because the deposit is held.” This means that the next one can say to him that the alien is dead, and that the remaining is simple and therefore the apostate is exalted in his sight:

mechaber.he: רועה כהן שנתן בהמות בחצר בעל הבית וילדה אחת מהן בכור ונתערב עם של בעל הבית ומת אחד מהם הוי ליה בעל הבית מוחזק ויאכלנו במומו:
mechaber.en: A kohen shepherd who placed animals in the owner's courtyard and one of them bore a firstborn and it became mixed with the owner's animals and one of them died—the house-owner is in possession and eats it in its blemished state.

siftei_kohen.he: הוי ליה בעל הבית מוחזק כו'. ולא אמרינן כיון שהכהן הוא רועה שלו ודאי הקנה לו חצרו כדי שיקנה הכהן את הבכור מיד כשיולד כי ניחא ליה למיעבד מצוה זו גם בממונו שיגדלו בכורותיו של כהן בחצרו וה"ל כשנים שהפקידו דלעיל סעיף א' אלא במקום פסידא לא אמרינן דניחא למיעבד מצוה כו' והבעל הבית עדיין מוחזק בו:
siftei_kohen.en: The owner of the house is held. And he did not say that the priest was his shepherd, of course, he had given him his court so that the priest would give him the first one immediately when he was born, that he had the privilege of this mitzvah, and that he would grow up in the hands of Cohen in his garden and the “for when the clerk had been poisoned by section A, but instead of the loss, he did not say that he had been enslaved to whom the house was still held.”

turei_zahav.he:
רועה כהן. פי' רועה שהוא כהן:
הוי ליה בעל הבית מוחזק כו'. בטור כתוב לא אמרינן כיון שהוא רועה כו' פירוש על פי הגמ' דאיתא ר' טרפון סבירא ליה אקנויי מקנה ליה בחצירו וניחא ליה דליתעביד מצוה והוה ליה כשנים שהפקידו אצל רועה שמניח ביניהם ומסתלק פרש"י אקנויי מקנה ליה בעל הבית לכהן מקום בחצרו כדי שיזכה כהן בבכורות כשיולדו מיד דתקנה ליה חצרו דניחא ליה לאינש דליתעבד מצוה בממוניה שיגדלו בכורותיו של כהן בחצרו והוה ליה חצר של שניהם וכאלו שנים הפקידו אצלו הלכך חולקין דברשות שניהם עומד קמ"ל דלא אמרינן הכי אלא כר"ע דאמר כיון דאית ליה פסידא לב"ה אם מקנה ליה בחצרו לא מקנה ליה כלום והוי ליה כאחד שהפקיד אצל בעל הבית שהמוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה כ"ה בבכורות:
turei_zahav.en:
A kohen shepherd. Meaning a shepherd who is a kohen.
The owner is considered in possession. Rabbi Tarfon reasoned that an owner grants the kohen a share in his courtyard so that the kohen will immediately acquire firstborn animals born there, because a person wishes a mitzvah to be performed with his property. The courtyard would then be jointly owned, like property deposited by two people, and the animals divided. The law follows Rabbi Akiva: because granting a share would cause the owner loss, he does not do so, and the case is like one claimant seeking to remove property from the owner's possession. The burden of proof therefore rests on the claimant. [Citation 5.]

baer_heitev.he: מוחזק. ולא אמרינן כיון שהכהן הוא רועה שלו ודאי הקנה לו חצרו כדי שיקנה הכהן את הבכור מיד כשיולד כי ניחא ליה למיעבד מצוה זו גם בממונו שיגדלו בכורותיו של כהן בחצרו וה"ל כשנים שהפקידו דלעיל בס"א אלא במקום פסידא לא אמרינן דניחא ליה למיעבד מצוה וכו' והבעה"ב עדיין מוחזק בו והמע"ה עכ"ל הש"ך:
baer_heitev.en: In possession. We do not presume that because the kohen is his shepherd, the owner surely granted him rights in the courtyard so that the kohen would acquire the firstborn immediately upon its birth. Although the owner may wish to perform this mitzvah even at his own expense by raising the kohen's firstborn animals in his courtyard, as in the case above of two people who deposited animals, we do not presume such willingness where it causes a loss. The owner therefore remains in possession, and the burden of proof rests upon the claimant. Shach. Reference 5.

beer_hagolah.he: אוקימתא דרבא וכו' פלוגתא דרבי טרפון ור' עקיבא וכר"ע:
beer_hagolah.en: The ruling of Rava, etc., and the dispute of Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva, and the ruling follows Rabbi Akiva.

pitchei_teshuva.he:
ונתערב. [עיין בת' חתם סופר סי' ש"ז אודות בכור שנתערב והמעשה היה שהיהודי עשה סימן בבכור בצמרו שלא יתערב ומסרו לרועה עובד כוכבים בתוך עדרו והודיעו שזהו בהמת קדשים האסורה בגיזה ובהגיע שעת גז צאנו גזז הרועה את כל הצאן וגם הבכור וממילא שוב אין היכר וסימן מבכור והרי הוא נתערב בין כל העדר עוד זאת עשה הרועה שסירס הרבה מן הצאן וספק אם הבכור מן המסורסים או מן התמימים. והנה צריך לדון בכאן א' על התמימים שהם כולם ספק בכור תם וירעו כולם עד שיסתאבו ואם להתיר ע"י פריש כבר ידוע פלוגתת ר"ת ור"י כו' (עי' לעיל סי' ק"י ס"ו בט"ז וש"ך) והכא דבקדשים קיימינן כל אפין שוין דלא מהני פירש א' מהן דגזרינן שמא יקח מן הקבוע. ב' יש לדון על המסורסים ע"י הרועה והנה מעשה זה מספיק להתיר בכור לאכלו במומו עש"ך סי' שי"ג סק"ו והשתא שספק בכור הוא הרי כולם נאכלים לישראל דאמרינן לכהן אייתי ראיה שזה בכור הוא חוץ מאחד מהם שנותן לכהן משום גזל השבט אך לענין גיזה ועבודה מאחר דמ"מ בכולם יש בהן ספק בכור ואסורים בגיזה ועבודה לעולם כו' ע"ש שהעלה מאחר דאין ברור לנו שנתערב בכור בין העדר כי היהודי לא ראה זאת ורק הרועה אומר כן ודבריו אינם אלא דברי תימה לומר ששינה מה שציוה לו בעה"ב ובלא"ה נמי ידוע שעובד כוכבים אינו נאמן לא להתיר ולא לאסור עש"ך סי' קכ"ז סק"כ ואע"ג שאנו רואים שמספר הצאן הגזוזים הם כמו שהיה עם הבכור מ"מ דלמא אחרינא הוא ונהי דס"ס לא הוו לומר על כל א' שמא לא נתערב בכור כלל ואת"ל נתערב שמא אינו זה. דהרי אינו יכול להתהפך וכאן א"צ לדון תחלה אם היה כאן בכור דודאי היה כאן בכור עכ"פ מידי ספיקא לא נפקא. ולזאת יש למצוא קולא באותן שהוממו להתירן בגיזה ועבודה על א' משני אופנים. אופן א' שיתן א' מהם לכהן כדינו והכהן ישחטנו ויאכלנו כי מצוה עליו לאכלו ולמהר המצוה עדיף ומכיון שנשחט זו הותרו כולם בגיזה ועבודה כדלעיל סי' ק"י ס"ז בנאכל א' מהם וכאן אין עושה להדיא כדי לבטלם רק הכהן אוכל את שלו כמצותו אלא שלפ"ז לא יגוזו הנותרים אלא שנים שנים ולא אחד אחד כמבואר שם. אופן הב' שנסמך על רמ"א שם ס"ו להפריש כולם ביחד שלא ישארו הקבועות במקומם ואז מותר אפילו פירש בפנינו ויקח הנפרשים אז ומותרים לגוז אפי' אחד אחד אע"ג שחזרו אח"כ לקביעותן כמ"ש הש"ך שם רק שנים האחרונים יהיו אסורים ולזה יצורף ההיתר דלעיל שישחט א' מהנפרשים ואז נימא דהנשחט היה הבכור ועי"ז הותרו גם שנים האחרונים וגם בהתמין הנשארים יש למצוא קולא לא מבעיא אם הם מיעוטין והרוב נסתרסו די"ל איסורא ברוב הנסתרסים היה וכל התמין מותרים להדיא כו' ובפרט כיון שנסתרסו קודם שנודע התערובות ה"ל פירש קודם שנולד הספק ולא גזרינן שמא יקח מן הקבוע אלא אף אם הם רובא או חצין דלא שייך היתר הנ"ל. מ"מ אם יעקרו כולם ממקום קביעותם יש להתיר ע"פ הדרך הנ"ל גבי בעלי מומין כו' ומ"מ מהיות טוב אם אפשר לאחר שפירשו אחד אחד טוב לגרום להם מום מובהק ע"י עובד כוכבים ונאכלים אח"כ במומן ומהו מום מובהק ע' לעיל סי' ש"ט וכל מום צריך שיראה לג' בני הכנסת ולא יותר ע"פ יחיד עש"ב ומש"ש עוד בענין הגיזה שנתערב כתבתי לעיל סי' ש"ח ס"ח]:

סי' ש"ח ס"ח]:
pitchei_teshuva.en:
And it became mixed. See Responsa Chatam Sofer, siman 307, concerning a firstborn that became mixed with a flock. The Jew had placed a mark in the animal's wool to prevent confusion and entrusted it to a non-Jewish shepherd among the flock, informing him that this was a consecrated animal forbidden in shearing. When the time for shearing arrived, the shepherd sheared the entire flock, including the firstborn, so its distinguishing mark was lost and it became mixed among the whole flock. In addition, the shepherd castrated many animals, and it was uncertain whether the firstborn was among the castrated or the intact animals. There are two issues. First, all the intact animals are doubtful unblemished firstborns and should graze until they develop blemishes. The known dispute between Rabbeinu Tam and Rabbeinu Yitzchak about permitting an item that separated from a fixed mixture does not help here, because when consecrated animals are involved all agree that separation of one does not help, lest one take directly from the fixed mixture. Second, one must consider the animals castrated by the shepherd. Such an act is sufficient to permit a firstborn for eating once blemished. Since here each animal is only a doubtful firstborn, all may be eaten by an Israelite, because the kohen must prove that a particular animal is a firstborn, except that one animal must be given to a kohen because of the tribe's monetary claim. Yet regarding shearing and work, since each remains a possible firstborn, all would seemingly remain prohibited forever. The Chatam Sofer ultimately rules leniently because it was never established with certainty that the firstborn became mixed into the flock. The Jew did not see this; only the shepherd said so, and the shepherd's story itself is surprising, since it assumes he violated the owner's explicit instructions. In any event a non-Jew is not believed either to permit or to prohibit, as Shach writes in siman 127, seif katan 20. Although the number of shorn animals appears to match the number of animals including the firstborn, perhaps another animal was substituted. This does not create a full double doubt for each animal, because the doubts cannot be reversed in order and we already know that a firstborn existed somewhere. Nevertheless, the case remains doubtful. He therefore proposes two ways to permit the blemished animals for shearing and work. First, one animal should be given to a kohen as required. The kohen should slaughter and eat it, since eating the firstborn is his mitzvah and performing the mitzvah promptly is preferable. Once that animal is eaten, all the others become permitted for shearing and work, like the rule in siman 110, seif 7, where one item from the mixture was eaten. Here the act is not done explicitly in order to nullify the prohibition, because the kohen is simply eating his own animal as a mitzvah. According to this route, however, the remaining animals should be shorn only two at a time, not singly, as explained there. Second, one may rely on the Rama in siman 110, seif 6, by moving all the animals together so that none remains in its original fixed location. Then even separation in our presence is effective. The separated animals may be taken and shorn individually, even if they later return to a fixed group, as the Shach explains there, though the final two would remain prohibited. To solve that problem, one of the separated animals can be slaughtered, and we may say that the slaughtered one was the firstborn, thereby permitting the final two as well. A leniency can also be found for the remaining intact animals. If they are a minority and most of the flock was castrated, one may say the prohibition was among the majority that were castrated and the intact animals are permitted. This is especially so because the castration occurred before the mixture became known, which is like separation before the doubt arose, where the decree against taking from the fixed mixture does not apply. Even if the intact animals are the majority or exactly half, so that this argument is unavailable, if all are removed from their fixed location one may permit them by the same method described for the blemished animals. As an added precaution, if possible, after they separate one by one it is proper to have a non-Jew cause an unmistakable blemish in them; they may then be eaten because of that blemish. For the definition of an unmistakable blemish see siman 309. Every blemish must be inspected by three members of the congregation and may not be permitted by one person alone. See there. His discussion of the mixed fleece is cited above in siman 308, seif katan 8.
And it became mixed. [See the responsum Chatam Sofer siman 307 regarding a firstborn that became mixed up. The case was: a Jew made a mark on the firstborn with its wool so it would not become mixed, and handed it to a non-Jewish shepherd within his flock, informing him that this was a consecrated animal forbidden to be shorn. When the time came to shear his flock, the shepherd sheared all the animals including the firstborn, and thereby the distinguishing mark was gone and the firstborn became mixed among the entire flock. Furthermore, the shepherd castrated many of the flock, and it is doubtful whether the firstborn is among those castrated or among the unblemished ones. Now there are two issues to discuss: First, regarding the unblemished ones — they are all in a state of doubtful firstborn, and all must graze until they become blemished. As for whether to permit via separation (perish), the dispute of Rabbeinu Tam and Ri is already known (see above siman 110 se'if 6 in Taz and Shakh), and here where we are dealing with consecrated animals all opinions are equal — separation does not help, for we decree lest one take from the fixed group. Second, there is discussion regarding those castrated by the shepherd. This act is sufficient to permit the firstborn to be eaten with its blemish (see Shakh siman 313 se'if katan 6). Now that it is a doubtful firstborn, all of them may be eaten by Israelites — for we say to the kohen: bring proof that this is a firstborn, except for one of them which is given to the kohen so as not to steal from the tribe. However, regarding shearing and working — since all of them bear the doubt of firstborn, they are forever forbidden for shearing and working, etc. He concludes: since we are not certain that a firstborn became mixed into the flock — for the Jew did not see this and only the shepherd says so, and his words are nothing but astonishing, to say he changed what the master had commanded him; and furthermore it is known that a non-Jew is not believed either to permit or to forbid (see Shakh siman 127 se'if katan 20) — and even though we see that the number of shorn animals is as it was with the firstborn, nevertheless perhaps another animal replaced it, and even a double doubt does not apply here — to say of each one: perhaps no firstborn became mixed at all, and even if it did become mixed, perhaps this is not it — for it cannot switch; and here there is no need first to determine whether a firstborn was present, since a firstborn certainly was there, but at any rate it does not emerge from doubt. Therefore one may find a leniency for those that were blemished to permit them for shearing and working, in one of two ways. First way: give one of them to the kohen as is proper, and the kohen slaughters and eats it — for he is commanded to eat it and hastening a mitzvah is preferable. Once this one is slaughtered, all the rest become permitted for shearing and working, as per above siman 110 se'if 7 where one of a group is eaten. Here he is not acting explicitly to nullify them — the kohen is simply eating his own as his mitzvah requires — except that according to this the remaining ones may only be shorn two at a time, not one at a time, as stated there. Second way: rely on the Rema there se'if 6 to separate them all together so that the fixed ones are no longer in their place, whereupon it is permitted even if they were separated before us, and one may take the separated ones and they are permitted for shearing even one at a time, even if they returned afterward to their fixed place, as the Shakh writes there — except the last two would remain forbidden. To this may be added the leniency above: slaughter one of the separated ones, and then we say the one slaughtered was the firstborn, thereby permitting even the last two. And regarding the unblemished remaining ones there is also leniency to be found — not only if they are a minority and the majority were castrated can we say the prohibition was among the majority castrated and all the unblemished are permitted; but also particularly since they were castrated before the mixture became known, they are like "separated before the doubt arose," and we do not decree lest one take from the fixed group. Even if they are a majority or half, which does not apply the leniency mentioned above — nonetheless if they are all uprooted from their fixed place one may permit them by the above method as for the blemished ones, etc. Furthermore, from the best, if possible, after they have been separated one by one, it is good to arrange a conspicuous blemish via a non-Jew and they may then be eaten with their blemish. What constitutes a conspicuous blemish — see above siman 309. Every blemish must be seen by three members of the community and not [ruled upon] by one individual alone, as stated there. And what he wrote further regarding the wool that became mixed — I wrote about that above siman 308 se'if 8.]
